# The exact first-order information from a free mixture parameter

Let Q be a nonempty compact convex set in R^d, p a point, and
Z=conv({p} union Q). Consider y=(1-t)p+tq with q in Q and 0<t<1.
Use the minimizing normal cone

    N_Q^min(q)={u:u dot(q'-q)>=0 for every q' in Q}.

Then the exact identity is

    N_Z^min(y)=N_Q^min(q) intersect (q-p)-perp.         (1)

To prove it, suppose u minimizes on Z at y. Since p,q are in Z,
both u dot p and u dot q are at least u dot y. Their strict convex
combination with coefficients 1-t,t equals u dot y. Both must equal
that value. Thus u dot(q-p)=0, and comparison with all of Q gives
u in N_Q^min(q). Conversely these two properties imply that u has
the same value on p and q and no smaller value anywhere in Q. By
linearity it has no smaller value anywhere in their convex hull,
proving (1).

Apply this with p=g_B and
Q={(g_A+g_sigma)/2:0<=sigma<=1_C dx, sigma(C)=a}.
At the interior-mixture actual maximizer from
`candidate 005bedbecd71db6d`, the averaged
coarea-weighted cap normal is therefore subject to exactly two kinds
of first-order conditions:

1. it minimizes over Q, selecting the unique lower a-volume cap of C
   when the normal is nonzero;
2. it is orthogonal to the segment direction q-g_B.

The second is precisely the radial equality already proved there.
Identity (1) is an equality of full normal cones, not merely a necessary
condition obtained from one parameterization. Consequently allowing
arbitrary simultaneous infinitesimal changes of the selector measure
and the interior mixture coefficient yields no additional independent
first-order normal-cone condition.

The radial equality can equivalently be expressed as a positive balance
of the radial slopes of the actual active caps. In the strict-bad-depth
setting of the cited note every active cap excludes exactly one of p,q:
it cannot contain both, and it passes through their strict mixture.
Thus all radial slopes are nonzero, and both signs must occur in a
positively weighted balance. This is a consequence, not a new equation.

There is no automatic second-order identity for a minimum of active cap
functions. Already min(D+t+At^2,D-t+Bt^2) has a strict local maximum at
t=0 for every finite A,B, despite its opposite first derivatives and
their balanced average. Thus arbitrary individual second derivatives
can coexist with the radial maximum. Any stronger second-order argument
would need additional geometric information about the actual cap
functions; it does not follow merely from freeing the mixture parameter.
